- When sentiment turns positive (≥0.2) or shows a recent spike, reduce forecasted overshoots by 5–10% to avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment.
- If the model consistently forecasts higher prices than true outcomes (especially in early 30d window), apply a downward bias correction of 2–5% for the first 5–7 days of the forecast horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecasted decline by 1–3% to allow for mean reversion without excessive sell-off.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) or shows strong bearish momentum, model often underestimates downside — increase forecasted lows by 2–4% to account for sentiment-driven volatility.
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show a clear downward trend, reduce forecasted highs by 3–6% to reflect mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.2) and history shows low volatility, model tends to overestimate short-term moves — cap forecast range within ±2% of recent 7-day average.
